qa.question: If I have a Digimon with this Digimon in digivolution cards, and the only other card I have is a token, can I <Draw 1> with this card's [When Attacking] inherited effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If that token is a Digimon, you can <Draw 1>.

qa.question: If the 3 cards revealed for this card's [On Play] effect include only either 1 card with the [Puppet] trait or 1 card with the [LIBERATOR] trait, can I just add that 1 card to my hand?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
Even if you only reveal one of the applicable cards, you can still add it to your hand.

qa.question: If the 3 cards I reveal from my deck for this card's [On Play] effect include both a card with [Puppet] trait and 1 card with the [LIBERATOR] trait, can I choose to only add one of them to my hand, and place the remaining cards at the bottom of my deck?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
If you have cards that are targets of this effect, you must add as many cards to your hand as possible.

changes.before: ⟨Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)⟩ (At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or other [Puppet] trait Digimon, this Digimon may attack a player without suspending.)
changes.after: ⟨Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)⟩ (At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or other [Puppet] trait Digimon, this Digimon attacks a player without suspending.)

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Security] effect to play a Tamer card with the [LIBERATOR] trait and a play cost of 4 or less?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
You can play it as long as the card has the [LIBERATOR] trait and a play cost of 4 or less.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Security] effect to play a Digi-Egg card with the [LIBERATOR] trait?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can't play it because Digi-Egg cards don't have play costs.

qa.question: If this card is checked from a security stack, does its [Security] effect activate, then does it battle with the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, its [Security] effect activates, then it battles.

qa.question: Does this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect count both my Digimon and my opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer:
Yes, it does.
If there are 3 or more total Digimon between you and your opponent, you further reduce this DP-reducing effect by 3000.

qa.question: What does "it further gets -3000 DP" in this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect mean, exactly?
qa.answer: If the conditions are met, the -3000 DP effect will further get -3000 DP for a total reduction of -6000 DP for 1 of your opponent's Digimon.

qa.question: What does "when [...] would leave the battle area" in this card's [All Turns] inherited effect mean, exactly?
qa.answer: "When [...] would leave the battle area" refers to when this Digimon is placed in the trash, returned to the hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to the breeding area, or placed under another card.

changes.before: ⟨Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)⟩ (At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or other [Puppet] trait Digimon, this Digimon may attack a player without suspending.)
changes.after: ⟨Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)⟩ (At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or other [Puppet] trait Digimon, this Digimon attacks a player without suspending.)

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

qa.question: [Familiar] Tokens have an [On Deletion] effect, but because tokens are removed from the game instead of being placed in the trash when deleted, does this mean that the [On Deletion] effect doesn't activate?
qa.answer: Tokens aren't placed in the trash when deleted, but [On Deletion] effects on tokens will activate as if the token was a Digimon.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect to place a BT11-063 [Geremon] or BT15-035 [Geremon] from my trash in this card's digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
BT11-063 [Geremon] and BT15-035 [Geremon] have a rule that also treats them as having the name [Numemon], therefore you can place them as digivolution cards under this Digimon.

qa.question: When effects play multiples of my Tokens and/or Digimon with the [Puppet] trait, can I use this card's [Your Turn] effect to give <Rush> to all of the played Digimon by suspending this Tamer?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can only specify 1 Digimon that will gain <Rush> from among multiple Digimon that were played at the same time.

qa.question: Does "if there are 3 or more Digimon" in this card's [Main] effect count both my Digimon and my opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer:
Yes, it does.
If there are 3 or more total Digimon between you and your opponent, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -12000 DP.

qa.question: What does "it further gets -6000 DP" in this card's [Main] effect mean, exactly?
qa.answer: If the conditions are met, the -6000 DP effect will further get -6000 DP for a total reduction of -12000 DP for 1 of your opponent's Digimon.

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0224.title: <Recovery>
comprehensive-0224.text:
16-6. <Recovery>
16-6-1. <Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.
16-6-2. <Recovery> effects execute processing.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0227.title: <Jamming>
comprehensive-0227.text:
16-9. <Jamming>
16-9-1. <Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.
16-9-2. <Jamming> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0229.title: <Reboot>
comprehensive-0229.text:
16-11. <Reboot>
16-11-1. <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-2. <Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-11-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-4. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is mandatory.
16-11-5. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.

comprehensive-0233.title: <Rush>
comprehensive-0233.text:
16-15. <Rush>
16-15-1. <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.
16-15-2. <Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0236.title: <Decoy>
comprehensive-0236.text:
16-18. <Decoy>
16-18-1. <Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.
16-18-2. <Decoy> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when another of your Digimon specified by this effect would be deleted by an opponent's effect (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-18-3. "By deleting this Digimon" in <Decoy> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "<Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted" will be mandatory.

comprehensive-0237.title: <Armor Purge>
comprehensive-0237.text:
16-19. <Armor Purge>
16-19-1. <Armor Purge> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with <Armor Purge> would be deleted, by trashing the top card of the Digimon with this effect, this effect prevents the deletion.
16-19-2. <Armor Purge> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-19-3. "By trashing the top card of the Digimon" in <Armor Purge> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

comprehensive-0244.title: <Barrier>
comprehensive-0244.text:
16-25. <Barrier>
16-25-1. <Barrier> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle, by trashing the top card of your security stack, this effect prevents that deletion.
16-25-2. <Barrier> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-25-3. "By trashing the top card of your security stack" in <Barrier> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

comprehensive-0253.title: <Overclock>
comprehensive-0253.text:
16-34. <Overclock>
16-34-1. <Overclock> is a keyword effect. At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or 1 of your other specified Digimon, the Digimon with this effect attacks a player without suspending. This is shown on cards using text such as <Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)>.
16-34-2. <Overclock> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the end of your turn. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-34-3. "By deleting 1 of your Tokens or 1 of your other specified Digimon" in <Overclock> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "the Digimon with this effect attacks a player without suspending" will be mandatory.
